page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-24GB is an x86_64 cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. It is provisioned with 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction extensions such as AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is configured at 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data, and features no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid general-purpose compute characteristics alongside some shared-resource constraints. In Geekbench, the instance achieves a strong single-core score of 2062.0 and a multi-core score of 8339.0, excelling notably in text processing at 2948.0. PassMark evaluation registers a CPU score of 12023.12, database operations at 3305.9, and Redis SET throughput at 8.75 million operations per second. However, under intensive synthetic load, the stress-ng multi-core metric lands in the lower quartile at 4685.03, and the PassMark memory score rates in the bottom 25 percent at 1446.47. In addition, static web serving throughput measures at 4.63 GB/sec.

Given its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation and shared CPU model, this server offers a cost-efficient resource tier for workloads that do not continuously saturate CPU execution units. It is well matched for mid-sized containerized services, microservices backends, text processing pipelines, internal continuous integration workers, and general application hosting where dedicated hardware isolation is not critical.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-24GB is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 6 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory balance. The configuration includes no local storage or discrete graphics hardware, requiring external volumes for persistent file systems. Performance metrics show competitive Geekbench text processing and balanced multi-core execution, alongside average database operations and Redis SET throughput of 8.75 million operations per second. Synthetic stress tests and memory bandwidth benchmarks show performance drops typical of shared virtualization environments. This instance is best suited for application hosting, containerized microservices, build pipelines, and mid-tier background processing jobs.
